newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bols 1996 profit falls, sees 1997 uptick.
newsitem.headline: Bols 1996 profit falls, sees 1997 uptick.

text.p: BolsWessanen NV said on Thursday 1996 net profit from normal operations fell 9.2 percent, slightly better than its own forecast of a 10 percent fall, and predicted a 1997 operating improvement.

The food and drink group's net from normal operations in 1996 fell to 184.2 million guilders from 202.9 million while turnover crept up to 4.69 billion guilders from 4.63 billion. The dividend was maintained at 1995's 1.28 guilders per share.
Share analysts had anticipated net profits of 181 million from BolsWessanen.
"For all four products groups the 1997 operating result is expected to be higher than in 1996," the company said in a statement with the results.
"The executive board expects that, in the absence of unforeseen circumstances, net income per share from ordinary activities in 1997 will increase," it added.
The firm reported 1996 net income per share from normal operations of 2.19 guilders, down from 2.43 guilders.

BolsWessanen said it expects its associates' income to grow slightly in the current year but the tax burden is expected to increase and interest charges will also rise as a result of takeovers and joint ventures which were sealed in 1996.

Investments in fixed assets will total 120 million guilders in 1997, slightly down from last year's 122.9 million. The investments will be financed from the company's existing funds, BolsWessanen said.
